sections.name: File setup, prepared, evidence, fact, raw, MemoryRepository
sections.title: Test file setup and sample data
sections.what: Brings in the extraction functions and test tools, and defines a sample land record, a helper that builds a quote with its positions, a helper that builds a fact, and a memory repository that stores results in a list.
sections.why: Gives every test the same known input.

sections.name: AI extraction trust boundary
sections.title: Trust boundary checks
sections.what: Checks that identifiers must match their quote, numeric equivalents of area are accepted while wrong numbers are rejected, normalized names and document types are accepted, and malformed offsets and incomplete output are rejected. Also checks that successful and failed runs are saved and counted, that a missing OpenAI key raises a configuration error, and that the prompt contains the required rules.
sections.why: These are the main safety checks for AI output.
sections.watch_out: Part of the metric-recording check was cut off in the packet, so its full assertions could not be confirmed here.

sections.name: configured extraction providers
sections.title: Configured provider checks
sections.what: Checks that Gemini output goes through the same grounding check and is saved with its details, that malformed output and provider outages are saved as failed attempts, and that the provider must be named explicitly with its matching key present.
sections.why: Confirms that every AI provider is held to the same rules and that failures are visible.
sections.watch_out: The provider selection check was partly cut off in the packet, so its exact assertions could not be confirmed here.

summary: Tests the AI extraction step: that only facts backed by exact quotes are accepted, that failures are recorded, that Gemini and OpenAI are configured correctly, and that the provider must be chosen explicitly.
purpose: Protects the rule that AI output is never trusted without evidence in the source text.
why: Likely reason: AI output can be wrong or invented, so the boundary is tested heavily.
how: Uses a sample land record and helpers that build facts with quotes and positions. Fake providers and a memory repository let each test run without a real AI service or database. Tests then check accepted results, rejected results, saved records, and recorded metrics.
inputs: Sample text, fake provider responses, and environment settings.
risks: Fake providers replace the real AI clients, so network and API behavior are not tested here.
debug: If a grounding test fails, compare the quote, the offsets, and the value. If a provider test fails, check the fake client response shape against the real one.
